title: Tesla misled South Korean buyers over Full Self-Driving, consumer group alleges
body: The direct financial hit to Tesla is likely small, but the case adds to regulatory and reputational risk around Full Self-Driving, a product central to the company's valuation story. A cease-and-desist order or fines in a fast-growing market would be a setback. Refund claims would be a bigger issue if they spread to other countries selling China-built cars. The dispute also highlights how much Tesla's international software revenue depends on certification regimes it does not control, which matters as it pushes for approval in Europe. Investors will watch whether the regulator acts quickly and whether similar complaints emerge elsewhere. --- Tesla's South Korean boom was built on China-made cars, and a consumer group says the company sold their owners self-driving software they could never legally switch on.

title: PBOC is expected to set the USD/CNY reference rate at 6.6811 – Reuters estimate
body: Yesterday the PNoC made moves to slow the yuan appreciation: China's PBOC lifts FX reserve ratio to 6%: what it means for the yuan, AUD --- The People's Bank of China is due to set the daily USD/CNY reference rate at around 0115 GMT (2115 US Eastern time), a fixing that remains one of the most closely watched signals in Asian foreign exchange markets. China operates a managed floating exchange rate system, under which the renminbi (yuan) is allowed to trade within a prescribed band around a central reference rate, or midpoint, set each trading day by the PBOC. The current trading band permits the currency to move plus or minus 2% from the official midpoint during onshore trading hours. Each morning, the PBOC determines the midpoint based on a range of inputs. These include the previous day's closing price, movements in major currencies, particularly the US dollar, broader international FX conditions, and domestic economic considerations such as capital flows, growth momentum and financial stability objectives. The midpoint is not a purely mechanical calculation, allowing policymakers discretion to guide market expectations. Once the midpoint is announced, onshore USD/CNY is free to trade within the allowable band. If market pressures push the yuan toward either edge of that range, the central bank may step in to smooth volatility. Intervention can take the form of direct buying or selling of yuan, adjustments to liquidity conditions, or guidance through state-owned banks.

title: The very early results in Kentucky show a massive swing towards Democrats
body: I highlighted KY-06 as an early district to watch as a barometer of today's vote and now some real results are crossing and betting markets are moving. In Anderson County, the numbers show the Republican Alvarado leading by 19 percentage points. That's good, right? No, it's not because in the prior three House elections, the Republican won that county +48, +54 and +54. So that's around a 35-points swing towards the Democrat candidate with 49% of votes counted. In Montgomery County on the opposite side of the district, 43% of votes are counted and the patter is similar. It shows Alvarado up 16 points but that compares to +53 in the prior election, +54 in 2022 and +43 in 2020. In Jessamine County, with 27% of the vote, Dumbo leads +0.9% and that compares to R+46.3% in 2024, a huge swing. That's a smaller percentage of the vote but the raw number is triple the size of the other two counties that have reported. That looks like a Democratic landslide and prediction markets appear to endorse it. There has also been a notable move towards Democrats winning the Senate at 86% compared to 73% earlier today. For Kentucky, there is an important caveat here. Nearly all Kentucky counties are expected to report early and absentee votes in their first update, according to the Associated Press. Those numbers are likely from early and mail-in voters, which skew Democrat. Update: Likely the most-significant data point yet is in.

title: Trump says no immediate plan to strike Iran as Netanyahu hints at attack this week
body: Trump's remarks could take some heat out of crude, as they reduce the near-term chance of a fresh US-led escalation that markets had begun to price after Netanyahu's hints. Any relief is likely to be limited, because oil's risk premium rests on the Strait of Hormuz, where Iranian attacks, the US blockade of Iranian ports and Monday's limited US strikes keep supply risk live. The bigger swing factor for oil is whether the Qatari-mediated talks produce a Hormuz deal, which would ease shipping risk far more than any single comment from Washington. A divergence between Trump and Netanyahu also leaves open the risk of Israeli action without full US backing, which would likely push prices sharply higher. If Trump is planning strikes he is doing well to keep his mouth shut about it. -- Trump is in no hurry to escalate with Iran, but Netanyahu is, and oil markets will be watching which of them sets the timetable.

title: BMW issues second profit warning, says car business could slip into operating loss
body: The warning adds pressure on European auto stocks heading into Frankfurt's open, with Mercedes-Benz and Volkswagen exposed to the same China weakness. The cut is partly self-inflicted, through faster restructuring and production ramp-up costs, so investors may treat it as less severe than a pure demand shock. The intact cash flow target supports that reading. Still, a margin range that includes a loss is a striking signal for a premium carmaker, and it could reinforce caution on the sector's China exposure. Wednesday's results will decide whether the selloff deepens or stabilises. --- BMW's car business could now lose money this year, though part of the damage comes from cutting jobs faster and building popular new models, not just from China. title: Central bank gold buying jumps 42% in Q3 as high prices hit jewellery demand, WGC says
body: The split in demand matters for price support: central banks tend to buy steadily rather than chase prices, so their stepped-up purchases act as a floor under gold in a way retail demand cannot. The weakness in jewellery and bar and coin buying shows gold's rally has relied more on institutional and official money than on households, leaving it more exposed if fund inflows reverse. The near-collapse in recycling at these prices is notable, as owners appear to be holding gold rather than selling, which tightens available supply. Investors should weigh the council's upbeat outlook against its position as an industry body funded by producers. --- Earlier: Gold trims gains after overnight strikes on Iran as the focus turns to the US midterm elections --- Central banks are buying gold faster than ever while households balk at the price, and that split is now doing much of the work holding up demand.

title: US warns of Houthi threat to Saudi airports and infrastructure, curbs travel to oil areas
body: For oil, the alert matters less for what has happened than for where Washington now sees risk. By naming Qatif and Yanbu, it points to the possibility of strikes on processing and export infrastructure, not just airports. That threat could support a geopolitical risk premium in Brent even without physical disruption. Yanbu is especially sensitive because it is Saudi Arabia's alternative export route if Gulf shipping is threatened, so any attack there would hit a key buffer for global supply. The wider risk-off backdrop could also lift demand for haven assets, while Gulf equities and airline stocks remain exposed to further disruption. --- Washington's latest Saudi alert reports no new strike, but it names the kingdom's oil heartland and its back-up export route as places its own staff should stay away from.

title: Carney says US trade talks to intensify as Washington asks less and offers mor
body: Carney's remarks offer modest support for the Canadian dollar, as any easing of the 50% US tariff would lift a weight on Canadian exporters and the growth outlook. title: Australian Dollar futures hit 2.5-week low after RBA rate hike.
